tests.topic: Sunday breakfast at the bar with Dad: Dad drinks his coffee standing at the counter, the child has a cornetto and a glass of warm milk and gets sugar on his nose.
Sunday lunch at the grandparents' house: the long table, who sits next to whom, the cousins at the small table, and Grandpa who falls asleep in the armchair afterwards.
A child's first day at nursery school (scuola dell'infanzia): a new backpack, a little fear at the door, and by the end of the morning a new friend who shares the same table.
A visit to the children's doctor when nothing hurts: she listens to the child's heart, looks in the mouth and ears, measures how tall he is, and gives him a sticker at the end.
The yellow school bus that stops in front of the child's house every morning: the driver is called Franco, the child always sits by the window, and the dog watches the bus leave.
A rainy day: the child puts on yellow boots to jump in the puddles, and when the rain stops there are snails on the garden wall.
Children play football in the courtyard after school: two backpacks make the goal, there is no referee, and the game stops when the ball rolls under a parked car.
The town band plays in the square on the day of the village festival: the drum is so loud that the child covers his ears at first, then he claps with everyone.
Grandpa's vegetable garden in summer: the tomatoes are red and the zucchini are big, the plants get water in the evening when the sun is low, and the child has a small watering can of her own.
A child goes to the baker's with Mum early in the morning: the shop smells good, Mum buys bread for lunch, the child pays with the coins, and the baker gives him a small piece of focaccia.
The postman who comes down the street on his scooter every morning: he puts letters in the boxes, today he has a big parcel for the child's family, and the neighbour's dog always barks at him.
The old fountain in the middle of the town square: the water is cold and good to drink, people sit around it in the evening, and the pigeons come to drink too.
A child talks with the librarian in the children's corner of the town library: the child wants a book about wolves, learns that it can go home with her for free, and must come back in two weeks.
A child looks at the moon from the bedroom window before sleeping: some nights it is round like a ball and some nights thin like a slice, and in the daytime the sun takes its place.
A child and Mum in the shoe shop: the old shoes are too small, the blue pair is too big, the red pair fits well, and the child wants to wear them out of the shop right away.
A child draws a picture for Grandma with crayons: a house, a yellow sun and a very big cat; Grandma says it is beautiful and puts it on the fridge door.
A very old castle on the hill above the town: long ago a lord lived there with his horses, now nobody lives in it, the walls are high, and children can visit it on Sunday.
A child and Grandma make fresh pasta on the kitchen table: Grandma names what goes in (flour and eggs, no water) and gives the child one small job, turning the handle of the pasta machine.
A girl describes her newborn baby brother: he is very small, sleeps almost all day and cries at night, and her job is to hold the towel at bath time.
The morning circle in a nursery class: the children sit on the floor around the teacher, each one says their name, and together they count who is here and who is at home today.
Brushing teeth every evening after dinner and before bed: the child's toothbrush is green and his sister's is red, a little toothpaste is enough, and Mum checks afterwards.
A train trip to the seaside with Mum: the ticket, the seat by the window, a long dark tunnel, and then suddenly the blue sea outside.
A child helps sort the rubbish at home: paper goes in one bin, glass in another, plastic in a third, and the banana peel goes in the small brown one under the sink.
A child's first swimming lesson at the pool: a cap and armbands, fear of putting her face in the water, and the teacher who holds her hands until she laughs.
The Christmas play at school: the child is dressed as a star and has only one line to say, the parents sit in the small chairs, and Dad takes too many photos.
Picking grapes in September at the uncle and aunt's vineyard: the adults cut the bunches and fill the baskets, and the child eats more grapes than he picks and ends up with sticky hands.

A child buys fruit alone for the first time at the market stall while Grandma watches: the child asks the fruit seller for four red apples, hears the price, pays two euros, and gets a cherry as a present.
The nursery class visits the fire station next to the school: the truck is red and has a long ladder, a firefighter lets the children try the helmet, and it is too big and heavy for them.
The apartment building where the child lives: the family is on the third floor, the lift is small, an old lady with a cat lives downstairs, and the balcony is full of flowers.
Grandpa reads Pinocchio aloud a little every evening: Pinocchio is a puppet made of wood, his nose gets long when he does not tell the truth, and that is the part the child likes best.
A small experiment at home: the child puts an ice cube in a glass on the sunny balcony and after a while there is only water; then the water goes into the freezer and is ice again the next day.
The school smock that Italian nursery children wear over their clothes: this child's is blue with her name on the pocket, it keeps paint off her jumper, and Mum washes it on Friday.
Painting at nursery school with hands: the child has yellow on one hand and blue on the other, presses them together, and is surprised to find green.
An old black-and-white photo of Grandpa as a child: he has short trousers and a bicycle, there is no television in his house, and he plays in the street with his brothers.
Every Saturday evening the family eats at the pizzeria: each person orders a different pizza, and the child always wants a margherita and eats the crust last.
Bedtime talk between a child and Mum: the child asks for one more story and a glass of water, Mum agrees to one short story and then turns off the big light but leaves the small one on.
A child and Dad pack the school backpack the evening before: the water bottle and the snack go in, the toy dinosaur has to stay at home, and the child is not happy about it.
Luca has a fever and stays home from school: he lies on the sofa with a blanket, is not hungry, drinks a lot of water, and Grandma comes to stay with him while his parents work.
A child who lives in Venice, where there are no cars and the streets are water: she goes to school by boat (vaporetto) with her father and likes to stand outside even when it is cold.
A child wakes up in a mountain village and everything outside is white and quiet: the car is under the snow, there is no school bus today, and the children build a snowman with a carrot nose.
Two children play hide-and-seek in the public gardens: they decide who counts to ten, one hides behind the big tree, and the other finds him because his red jacket shows.
A puppet show in the park on Sunday: the children sit on the grass, a puppet with a stick hides behind the curtain, and all the children shout to warn the other puppet.
A child on a farm goes to the hen house every morning with a basket: there are six hens, today there are four eggs, and one egg is still warm.
Anna's piggy bank: every Sunday Grandpa gives her a coin, she shakes the pig to hear how full it is, and she is saving for a new ball.
A child's father is a pizza maker and works in the evening: he leaves when the child eats dinner and comes home when she sleeps, so they play together in the morning.
A child sees the tower of Pisa for the first time: it is tall and white but not straight, the child is afraid it will fall, and Mum explains that it has stood like that for a very long time.
A child's favourite picture book about animals: the pictures are big and the words are few, the child cannot read yet but knows every page, and the last page has an elephant.
A bean on wet cotton wool in a glass on the classroom windowsill: the children give it a little water every day, first a small white root comes out, then a green leaf.
Getting dressed to go out on a cold winter morning: first the jumper, then the coat, the hat and the scarf, but the child can find only one glove; the other is in the coat pocket.
Two children make paper masks at school for Carnival and talk while they work: one makes a cat and the other a lion, they need the scissors and the orange pencil, and the teacher ties the elastic.
A child visits the Colosseum in Rome with her parents: it is very old, big and round, one side is lower because a piece is missing, and many people come from far away to see it.
A walk to the gelateria on a hot summer evening: the child picks two flavours, chooses a cone and not a cup, and has to eat fast because the gelato melts onto her hand.
An aunt who lives in another city by the sea: the child cannot visit often, so every Friday evening they talk on the phone screen and the aunt shows the sea from her window.
In autumn the teacher brings a basket of chestnuts to class and the children learn to count with them: one child has five, another has three, and they put them together.
A child falls while running in the park and scrapes a knee; Dad and the child talk: it hurts a little, Dad washes it with water at the fountain and puts on a plaster, and the child goes back to play.
A child and Mum wait at the tram stop in the city: the first tram is the wrong number, theirs is number 3, and the child wants to be the one who presses the button to get off.
A walk in the woods in autumn with Grandpa: the leaves are yellow and red and fall on the path, the child collects the biggest ones, and a squirrel runs up a tree with a nut.
The playground after school: there is a queue for the slide, so the child waits her turn, but what she likes best is the swing because Grandpa pushes her high.
The family sings in the car on the way to the grandparents: the child chooses the song, Mum knows all the words, Dad sings badly, and everybody laughs.
The olive harvest in November: big nets lie under the trees, the olives fall onto them, a tractor takes them to the mill, and the new green oil goes on a slice of bread.
